info.title: go-httpbin
info.description: A faithful Go port of httpbin.org — a simple HTTP request and response service useful for testing HTTP clients, debugging HTTP requests, and simulating various server behaviors.

get.description: Returns an HTML index page listing all available endpoints.
Returns the details of the incoming GET request, including query parameters, headers, origin IP, and the full URL.

post.description: Returns the details of the incoming POST request, including any body data (raw, JSON, form-encoded, or multipart).

put.description: Returns the details of the incoming PUT request, including any body data.

patch.description: Returns the details of the incoming PATCH request, including any body data.

delete.description: Returns the details of the incoming DELETE request, including any body data.

get.description: Returns the headers sent in the incoming request.
Returns the IP address of the client making the request. Respects `X-Forwarded-For` and similar proxy headers.
Returns the `User-Agent` header sent by the client.

user-agent.description: The User-Agent string from the request.

get.description: Returns the hostname of the server running go-httpbin.
Returns version and build information about the running go-httpbin instance.
Returns environment variables with the `HTTPBIN_` prefix that have been allowlisted by the server operator. If no variables have been allowlisted, returns an empty object.

env.description: Map of allowlisted HTTPBIN_ environment variable names to values, or null if none are configured.

get.description: Returns the incoming HTTP request in its raw HTTP/1.x wire format.

schema.example:
GET /dump/request HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
User-Agent: curl/8.4.0

get.description: Validates HTTP Basic Authentication credentials. Returns 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge header if credentials are missing or incorrect.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Expected username.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Expected password.

get.description: Like `/basic-auth`, but returns 404 instead of 401 when credentials are missing or incorrect, hiding the existence of the resource.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Expected username.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Expected password.

404.description: Missing or invalid credentials (deliberately obscures the 401)

get.description: Validates a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Returns 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge if the header is missing or malformed.
Validates HTTP Digest Authentication credentials using the given QoP and algorithm. Returns 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge on the first request (or when credentials are wrong).

parameters.name: qop
parameters.description: Quality of Protection. Only `auth` is currently supported.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Expected username.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Expected password.

get.description: Like `/digest-auth/{qop}/{user}/{password}` but with an explicit hash algorithm.

parameters.name: qop
parameters.description: Quality of Protection. Only `auth` is currently supported.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Expected username.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Expected password.

parameters.name: algorithm
parameters.description: Hash algorithm to use.

get.description: Returns a response with the specified HTTP status code. Accepts a single code or a comma-separated list of codes with optional weights for random selection (e.g. `200,301,500` or `200:0.8,500:0.2`). Certain status codes produce additional headers or bodies per the HTTP spec (e.g. 301 adds `Location`, 401 adds `WWW-Authenticate`).

parameters.name: codes
parameters.description: A single HTTP status code, or a comma-separated list of codes with optional weights (e.g. `200`, `200,404,500`, `200:0.7,500:0.3`).

post.description: Returns a response with the specified HTTP status code. See GET /status/{codes} for full description.

parameters.name: codes
parameters.description: A single HTTP status code, or a comma-separated weighted list.

put.description: Returns a response with the specified HTTP status code.

parameters.name: codes
parameters.description: A single HTTP status code in range [100, 599], or a comma-separated weighted list.

patch.description: Returns a response with the specified HTTP status code.

parameters.name: codes

get.description: Returns a 500 Internal Server Error with a configurable probability, or 200 OK otherwise. Useful for testing retry logic and error handling.

parameters.name: failure_rate
parameters.description: Probability of returning 500. Must be between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0.5.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random seed for reproducible results.

get.description: Issues a redirect chain of length `n`. By default uses relative redirects (via `/relative-redirect`); pass `absolute=true` to use absolute URLs (via `/absolute-redirect`). HTTP clients that follow redirects will ultimately receive a 200 from `/get`.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of redirects to perform. Must be >= 1.

parameters.name: absolute
parameters.description: If `true`, use absolute redirect URLs. Defaults to relative.

get.description: Performs `n` consecutive relative (path-only) 302 redirects. The final redirect points to `/get`. HTTP clients that follow redirects will ultimately receive a 200.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of redirects to perform. Must be >= 1.

get.description: Performs `n` consecutive absolute (full URL) 302 redirects. The final redirect points to `/get`. HTTP clients that follow redirects will ultimately receive a 200.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of redirects to perform. Must be >= 1.

get.description: Issues a redirect to the URL specified in the `url` query parameter, with an optional custom status code. If the server has a configured allowlist of redirect domains, the target domain must match.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to redirect to.

parameters.name: status_code
parameters.description: HTTP status code to use for the redirect. Must be in the 3xx range. Defaults to 302.

3XX.description: Redirect (or the status code you specified)

403.description: Target domain is not on the server's allowlist

post.description: Issues a redirect to the URL specified in the `url` query parameter.

3XX.description: Redirect (or whichever 3xx status code you specified)

default.description: Any other response from the redirect target

get.description: Returns all cookies sent in the request.

cookies.description: Map of cookie names to values.

get.description: Sets one or more cookies from query parameters, then redirects to `/cookies`. Each query parameter becomes a cookie with that name and value.

parameters.name: cookie_name
parameters.description: Each query parameter name/value pair becomes a cookie. (The parameter name shown here is illustrative — use any name.)

get.description: Deletes the cookies named by the query parameters, then redirects to `/cookies`.

parameters.name: cookie_name
parameters.description: Each query parameter name identifies a cookie to delete. The value is ignored.

schema.description: Cookie with expired Max-Age to effect deletion.

get.description: Returns a gzip-compressed JSON response containing request details. The `Content-Encoding: gzip` header is set.
Returns a deflate-compressed JSON response containing request details. The `Content-Encoding: deflate` header is set.
Brotli compression is not implemented in go-httpbin. Always returns 501 Not Implemented.

Returns a response whose headers are set from the query parameters. Each query parameter name becomes a response header name and its value becomes the header value. The headers are also reflected in the JSON response body. Setting `Content-Type` via a query parameter changes the response content type.

parameters.name: header_name
parameters.description: Each query parameter name/value pair becomes a response header. (The parameter name shown here is illustrative — use any valid header name.)

200.description: Response with the requested headers set

schema.description: The headers set on the response, reflected as a JSON object.

200.description: Response with the requested headers set

get.description: Returns 304 Not Modified if the request includes `If-Modified-Since` or `If-None-Match` headers. Otherwise returns a 200 with request details and sets `Last-Modified` and `ETag` response headers.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: Returns 304 if provided.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Returns 304 if provided.

get.description: Returns a response with a `Cache-Control: public, max-age={value}` header.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Number of seconds for `max-age`.

get.description: Returns a response with the given `ETag` header value. If the request includes `If-None-Match` matching the ETag, returns 304. If the request includes `If-Match` that does not match, returns 412.

parameters.name: etag
parameters.description: The ETag value to set on the response.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Returns 304 if this matches the ETag.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Returns 412 if this does not match the ETag.

get.description: Waits the specified duration before responding with request details. Accepts seconds as a float or any Go duration string (e.g. `500ms`, `1.5s`). The delay is capped at the server's configured maximum duration (default 10 seconds). If the client disconnects early, the server returns 499.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: Delay duration as seconds (float) or a Go duration string (e.g. `1s`, `500ms`).

499.description: Client closed request before the delay completed

get.description: Gradually streams a response body of the specified size over the specified duration. Useful for testing streaming clients, timeouts, and slow connection handling. Sets a fixed `Content-Length` (not chunked). A `Server-Timing` header reflects actual durations.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Total time to stream the response. Accepts a float (seconds) or Go duration string. Defaults to `2s`.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: Delay before streaming begins. Defaults to `2s`.

parameters.name: numbytes
parameters.description: Number of bytes to stream. Must be between 1 and the server's max body size. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: HTTP status code to return. Defaults to 200.

200.description: Streamed response (or the status code you specified)

default.description: Response with the status code specified by the `code` parameter.

1XX.description: Informational response with the status code specified by `code`.

3XX.description: Redirect response with the status code specified by `code`.

4XX.description: Client error response with the status code specified by `code`.

5XX.description: Server error response with the status code specified by `code`.

get.description: Returns `n` random bytes as binary data. The optional `seed` parameter makes the output reproducible.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of bytes to return. Must be between 0 and the server's max body size.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random seed for reproducible output.

get.description: Streams `n` random bytes in chunks using chunked transfer encoding. The optional `chunk_size` parameter controls how many bytes are sent per chunk (default 10240). The optional `seed` parameter makes the output reproducible.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Total bytes to stream. Must be between 0 and the server's max body size.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random seed for reproducible output.

parameters.name: chunk_size
parameters.description: Number of bytes per chunk. Defaults to 10240.

200.description: Chunked stream of random binary data

get.description: Decodes the URL-safe base64-encoded `value` and returns the raw bytes. An optional `content-type` query parameter sets the response `Content-Type`.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: URL-safe base64-encoded data to decode.

parameters.name: content-type
parameters.description: Content-Type to set on the response.

200.description: Decoded data. Content-Type is `application/octet-stream` by default, or whatever was passed in the `content-type` query parameter.

get.description: Encodes the given `value` using URL-safe base64 and returns the result.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Arbitrary data to encode.

parameters.name: content-type
parameters.description: Content-Type to set on the response.

get.description: Decodes the URL-safe base64-encoded `value` and returns the raw bytes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: URL-safe base64-encoded data to decode.

parameters.name: content-type
parameters.description: Content-Type to set on the response.

200.description: Decoded data. Content-Type is `application/octet-stream` by default, or whatever was passed in the `content-type` query parameter.

get.description: Streams `n` newline-delimited JSON objects, each containing request details with an incrementing `id` field. `n` must be between 1 and 100.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of JSON lines to stream. Must be 1–100.

get.summary: Stream JSON lines with timing control
get.description: Streams newline-delimited JSON objects with configurable count, total duration, initial delay, and per-line jitter. Each line contains an incrementing `id` and the timestamp it was sent.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of lines to stream. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Total duration over which to stream all lines. Must be >= 1s if provided.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: Initial delay before the first line is sent.

parameters.name: jitter
parameters.description: Fraction of the per-line interval to randomize. Between 0 (no jitter) and 1 (full jitter). Defaults to 0.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when this line was sent.

get.description: Streams Server-Sent Events (SSE) with configurable count, total duration, initial delay, and jitter. Each event is of type `ping` and includes a JSON data payload with an `id` and `timestamp`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of events to send. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Total duration over which to send all events. Must be >= 1s if provided.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: Initial delay before the first event is sent.

parameters.name: jitter
parameters.description: Fraction of the per-event interval to randomize. Between 0 and 1.

schema.description: A single SSE event. Each event has type `ping` and a JSON-encoded data payload.

get.description: Returns a chunked response whose HTTP trailers are set from the query parameters. Trailers are headers delivered after the response body. Certain trailer names are forbidden (e.g. `Authorization`, `Content-*`, `Host`).

parameters.name: trailer_name
parameters.description: Each query parameter name/value pair becomes an HTTP trailer. (The parameter name shown here is illustrative — use any allowed trailer name.)

get.description: Returns `numbytes` of content with full HTTP Range request support. Accepts `Range` headers for partial content and responds with 206 Partial Content or 416 Range Not Satisfiable. Sets `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges: bytes` headers.

parameters.name: numbytes
parameters.description: Total content length in bytes.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Standard HTTP Range header for requesting partial content (e.g. `bytes=0-1023`).

get.description: Returns a sample HTML page (an excerpt from Moby Dick).
Returns a sample JSON document.
Returns a sample XML document.

Returns an image whose format is determined by the `Accept` header. Supported types are `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, and `image/svg+xml`. Defaults to PNG if the `Accept` header is missing or wildcarded.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Desired image media type.

406.description: None of the requested media types are supported

415.description: Unsupported Media Type — Accept header does not match any supported image format

get.description: Returns an image of the specified format.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Image format to return.

get.description: Returns a randomly generated UUID v4.
Redirects to `/links/{n}/0`, which renders an HTML page with `n` links to other pages in the link chain.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of links to generate. Must be 0–256.

get.description: Returns an HTML page with `n` links pointing to other pages in the link chain. The `offset` parameter indicates the current page index.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Total number of links.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Current page index (0-based).

get.description: Returns an HTML page with a form that submits a POST request to `/post`.
Returns an HTML page containing a variety of UTF-8 characters for encoding testing.

post.description: Accepts a request body (any content type) and discards it, returning the number of bytes received along with the usual request details.

bytes_received.description: Number of bytes received in the request body.

get.description: Returns a standard `robots.txt` file that disallows `/deny`.
Returns a plain-text response. Listed in `/robots.txt` as disallowed so well-behaved bots do not crawl it.

Upgrades the connection to WebSocket protocol and echoes every received message back to the client. Useful for testing WebSocket clients. The connection is closed by the server after the client closes it.

parameters.name: max_fragment_size
parameters.description: Maximum WebSocket frame fragment size in bytes. Must be between 1 and the server's max body size.

parameters.name: max_message_size
parameters.description: Maximum WebSocket message size in bytes. Must be between 1 and the server's max body size.

Headers.description: Map of HTTP header names to their values (each value is a list of strings).

NoBodyResponse.description: Standard response for requests without a body (e.g. GET).

allOf.description: Standard response for requests that may include a body (e.g. POST, PUT).

data.description: Raw request body as a string (for non-form, non-JSON content types).

json.description: Parsed JSON body, if the request `Content-Type` was `application/json` and the body was valid JSON. `null` otherwise.

form.description: Form fields from a `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data` body.

files.description: File contents from a `multipart/form-data` body, keyed by field name.

authenticated.description: `true` if valid credentials were present in the request.

authorized.description: `true` if the credentials match the expected values.

user.description: The authenticated username, if credentials were valid.

detail.example: invalid value for parameter 'n': must be a positive integer

QueryParams.name: query_params
QueryParams.description: Any query parameters — they are echoed back in the `args` field of the response.

AnyBody.description: Any request body. go-httpbin accepts `application/json`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data`, and arbitrary binary/text bodies.

BadRequest.description: Bad Request — the request contained invalid parameters.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Method Not Allowed — the HTTP method is not supported by this endpoint.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Payload Too Large — the request body exceeds the server's configured maximum.

NotImplemented.description: Not Implemented — this endpoint is not implemented in go-httpbin.

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic Authentication. The credentials are validated against the username and password in the URL path.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token. Any non-empty token is accepted; the token value is echoed back in the response.

tags.name: HTTP Methods
tags.description: Endpoints that echo back the incoming request for specific HTTP methods.

tags.name: Anything
tags.description: Endpoints that echo back the incoming request for any HTTP method and arbitrary paths.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Endpoints for testing HTTP authentication schemes: Basic, Hidden Basic, Bearer, and Digest.

tags.name: Cookies
tags.description: Endpoints for inspecting, setting, and deleting cookies.

tags.name: Status Codes
tags.description: Endpoints that return specific HTTP status codes, optionally chosen randomly from a weighted list.

tags.name: Request Inspection
tags.description: Endpoints that return information about the incoming request or the server.

tags.name: Response Inspection
tags.description: Endpoints that control caching, ETags, and response headers.

tags.name: Response Formats
tags.description: Endpoints that return various content types: HTML, JSON, XML, images, links, and forms.

tags.name: Dynamic Data
tags.description: Endpoints that generate dynamic data: random bytes, UUIDs, delays, streaming, and range requests.

tags.name: Meta
tags.description: Endpoints providing metadata about the service: version, index page, robots.txt, and deny.
